Why does toast land butter-side down?
Why does toast land butter-side down?
It's not bad luck,
and it's not the weight
of the butter.
Mostly,
it's the height of your table.
As toast slides off
the edge,
it pivots on the rim
and starts to spin.
But the spin is slow,
and the fall is short:
from a table,
about 0.4 seconds.
In that time,
the toast only manages
about half a turn.
It started butter up.
Half a turn later:
butter down.
From a table about 3m
high,
it would spin a full
turn and land butter up.
So don't blame
the butter.
Blame the table.
